Projection, view and transformation matrices

Source: R/utils_opengl.R
opengl_matrices.Rd

The 4 x 4 homogeneous matrices of manim.utils.opengl.

Usage

matrix_to_shader_input(matrix)

orthographic_projection_matrix(
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  near = 1,
  far = OPENGL_DEPTH + 1,
  format_ = TRUE
)

perspective_projection_matrix(
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  near = 2,
  far = 50,
  format_ = TRUE
)

translation_matrix(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0)

x_rotation_matrix(x = 0)

y_rotation_matrix(y = 0)

z_rotation_matrix(z = 0)

opengl_rotation_matrix(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0)

rotate_in_place_matrix(initial_position, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0)

scale_matrix(scale_factor = 1)

view_matrix(translation = NULL, x_rotation = 0, y_rotation = 0, z_rotation = 0)

Arguments

matrix

A numeric matrix.

width, height

Size of the projected region.

near, far

Distances of the clipping planes.

format_

FALSE returns the matrix instead of its flattened form.

x, y, z

Translation distances or rotation angles in radians.

initial_position

A point.

scale_factor

Scale factor.

translation

Camera position; by default c(0, 0, 11).

x_rotation, y_rotation, z_rotation

Camera rotation angles.

Value

A 4 x 4 matrix, or a numeric vector of its 16 entries.

Details

  • translation_matrix(x, y, z), scale_matrix(scale_factor), x_rotation_matrix(x), y_rotation_matrix(y) and z_rotation_matrix(z) are the elementary transformations.

  • opengl_rotation_matrix(x, y, z) is the product of the rotations about the x, y and z axes (upstream calls it rotation_matrix inside manim.utils.opengl; here that name is the rotation about an axis, rotation_matrix()).

  • rotate_in_place_matrix(initial_position, x, y, z) moves initial_position to the origin, rotates, and moves back.

  • orthographic_projection_matrix() and perspective_projection_matrix() project the frame; width and height default to the frame size (a sixth of it for the perspective matrix).

  • view_matrix() is the inverse of the camera's model matrix.

  • matrix_to_shader_input(matrix) flattens a matrix column by column, the layout shaders take. The projection matrices return this form unless format_ = FALSE, and view_matrix() always does.

Examples

translation_matrix(1, 2, 3)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    1    0    0    1
#> [2,]    0    1    0    2
#> [3,]    0    0    1    3
#> [4,]    0    0    0    1
orthographic_projection_matrix(format_ = FALSE)
#>          [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,] 0.140625 0.00  0.0  0.0
#> [2,] 0.000000 0.25  0.0  0.0
#> [3,] 0.000000 0.00 -0.1 -1.1
#> [4,] 0.000000 0.00  0.0  1.0
